rfi.title: Southern African farmers prepare for powerful El Nino with agroecology
rfi.description: Farmer Dudzai Matsapa works under a scorching sun, digging small, shallow pits across his field in Nyanga, east of the Zimbabwean capital, Harare. He will later fill these potholes with organic manure and wait for the rainy season. This is all part of Matsapa’s preparation for the anticipated El Nino, which is expected to trigger drought and extreme heat across southern Africa.

rfi.title: The art of dressing: how clothes have shaped the image of the artist
rfi.description: How do you spot an artist? Are they the one with the jaunty beret or the dapper silk scarf? Or the tunic covered in paint? An exhibition at the Bourdelle Museum in Paris looks at how wardrobe choices have shaped society’s perception of artists – and made some of them into icons.

rfi.title: Nigeria's plan for state police raises hopes for security and fears of abuse
rfi.description: Nigeria this week took a step closer to a major overhaul of its security system after 28 of its 36 states approved a constitutional reform that would allow individual states to establish their own police forces. Supporters of the move say it will better protect against insecurity on a local level, but concerns have also been raised about the risk of abuse by state governors.

rfi.title: Suez Crisis at 70 reveals the humiliation France tried to keep hidden
rfi.description: Seventy years after France, the United Kingdom and Israel invaded Egypt following its nationalisation of the Suez Canal, the military operation is remembered as a diplomatic disaster. Friday marks the anniversary of a ceasefire that halted the fighting under international pressure, despite the invading forces' success on the battlefield. Archive footage excluded from French cinema newsreels shows the humiliation that followed, as Europe's colonial powers faced the limits of their influence.

france24fr.title: RDC : dialogue impossible entre Tshisekedi, Kabila et l'opposition ?
france24fr.description:
En République démocratique du Congo, la crise politique s'intensifie sur fond de guerre dans l'Est. La coalition d'opposition C64 souhaite rencontrer le président Félix Tshisekedi et son prédécesseur Joseph Kabila pour préparer un dialogue national. Mais Kinshasa menace de poursuites les opposants qui iraient rencontrer l'ancien chef de l'État à Goma, où il dirige désormais un mouvement politico-militaire intégrant l'AFC/M23.

Entre guerre, divisions politiques, débat sur la Constitution et élec

france24fr.title: Patronat et syndicats reçus lundi à Matignon : la colère va-t-elle retomber ?
france24fr.description:
Au menu de Présidentielle 2027: la conférence sociale organisée à Matignon, la démonstration de force de Jean-Luc Mélenchon et la cacophonie de la droite et du centre. 
 
Avec nos invités : Dorian Dreuil, expert associé à l'Observatoire de la vie politique de la Fondation Jean-Jaurès et Anthony Berthelier, journaliste politique au HuffPost.

france24fr.title: CNews : la pétition appelant à la fermeture de la chaîne dépasse le million de signatures
france24fr.description: Lancée pour réclamer la suppression de CNews de l'audiovisuel français, une pétition a dépassé dimanche le million de signatures. Mardi, les députés doivent se prononcer sur la suite à donner à cette initiative : classement sans suite ou examen de la demande.

france24fr.title: Samy Cohen: "Eisenkot est populaire car il représente un apaisement de la vie politique israélienne"
france24fr.description: En Israël, Gadi Eisenkot a été missionné par le président Herzog pour former le prochain gouvernement, dix jours après le résultat des législatives à l'issue desquelles aucune majorité claire ne s'est dégagée. La tâche de l'ancien chef d'Etat-major s'annonce particulièrement complexe. Il affiche sa détermination à réussir et tend même la main au Likoud de Benyamin Netanyahou. Samy Cohen, directeur de recherche émérite au CERI de Sciences Po, était l'Invité d'Au Cœur de l'Info.

france24fr.title: En Israël, Eisenkot invite le Likoud de Netanyahu à participer à une coalition
france24fr.description: Officiellement chargé dimanche de former le prochain gouvernement israélien, l'ex-haut gradé centriste Gadi Eisenkot a appelé à l'unité face à une "crise historique", dont il tient Benjamin Netanyahu pour responsable. Il s'est néanmoins dit ouvert à une coalition avec des élus du Likoud, mais aussi du parti d'extrême droite de Bezalel Smotrich.

france24fr.title: Tennis : Carlos Alcaraz remporte pour la première fois le Masters 1000 de Paris
france24fr.description: L'Espagnol Carlos Alcaraz, 3e joueur mondial, a décroché dimanche son premier titre au Masters 1000 de Paris en battant l'Américain Ben Shelton en finale. Avec ce 29e titre en carrière, il n'est plus qu'à une victoire d'égaler son grand rival Jannik Sinner, qui compte 30 trophées.

france24fr.title: Route du Rhum : "Franchement, c'est un rêve d'enfant", savoure Laperche
france24fr.description: "Franchement, c'est un rêve d'enfant. J'ai toujours vu des images incroyables des arrivées ici, celles des grands champions depuis des décennies. Mon rêve était de courir un jour dans cette catégorie reine des multicoques et de jouer la victoire au scratch" déclare Tom Laperche à son arrivée triomphante.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : Gadi Eisenkot officiellement chargé de former le prochain gouvernement en Israël
Débâcle de Trump aux midterms, revendications lycéennes, JOJ de Dakar : la semaine en images
france24fr.description: Retour sur les temps forts de l'actualité de la semaine écoulée et sur ses images les plus marquantes : la large victoire des démocrates américains aux élections de mi-mandat, la gronde des lycéens qui se poursuit partout en France et les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) de Dakar.

france24fr.title: Yémen : première livraison d'aide médicale du CICR dans la ville de Taëz
france24fr.description: Dr Pierre Catoire, médecin urgentiste vice-président de l'ONG Mehad, est notre invité.

france24fr.title: La Pologne en deuil confrontée au "terrorisme de l'intérieur"
france24fr.description: La Pologne en deuil s'est réveillée choquée dimanche, au lendemain de la tuerie perpétrée à Cracovie par un jeune "fasciné" par les idées d'extrême droite, qui a abattu six personnes et en a blessé quinze.

france24fr.title: Israël : Eisenkot, opposant à Netanyahu, au défi de former une coalition
france24fr.description: Charles Enderlin, journaliste et auteur, est notre invité.

france24fr.title: Inde : bougies, lanternes, et feux d'artifices pour fêter Diwali
france24fr.description: Les célébrations de Diwali ont débuté dimanche. À Ayodhya, considérée comme le lieu de naissance du seigneur Rama – la divinité vénérée lors de cette fête –, les célébrations comprenaient des spectacles inspirés de l’épopée hindoue « Ramayana », des spectacles de lumières et de lasers, des concerts, des feux d’artifice et des démonstrations de drones.

france24fr.title: Au large du Sénégal, au moins 34 personnes sont mortes dans le naufrage d'une pirogue de migrants
france24fr.description: Au moins 34 personnes ont péri dans le naufrage d'une pirogue de migrants au large de Kébémer, dans le nord-ouest du Sénégal, selon les médias publics sénégalais et une ONG. Les recherches se poursuivent pour retrouver d'éventuels survivants.

france24fr.title: Trump veut Dana White, patron de la fédération de MMA, comme porte-parole
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a annoncé samedi avoir proposé le poste de porte-parole de la Maison Blanche à Dana White, un de ses proches qui dirige l'UFC, principale organisation mondiale d'arts martiaux mixtes (MMA).

france24fr.title: "Non au data-center de Rantigny" : manifestation contre le développement de l'IA
france24fr.description: Une manifestation a été organisée pour dire non au futur projet de data center à Rantigny (Oise), ce samedi 7 novembre 2026, réunissant riverains et élus d’opposition.

france24fr.title: Budget pharaonique, révolution graphique... Cinq raisons qui font de "GTA VI" le jeu du siècle
france24fr.description: "Grand Theft Auto VI" débarque le 19 novembre sur Playstation et Xbox Series. Qualifié de "jeu du siècle", le nouvel opus du studio Rockstar occupe une place à part dans l'industrie vidéoludique, promettant d’être l'un des objets culturels les plus influents de ces dernières années. Retour sur les raisons d'un phénomène qui devrait tout emporter sur son passage.

zeit.description: CDU-Politiker Frei erteilt der Plastiksteuer eine Absage, Matthias Miersch von der SPD verweist auf Gespräche. Im Haushalt könnte ohne die Steuer ein Loch entstehen.

observador.title: VSC x FCP. “Decisões certas nas áreas valem nota 7”

observador.title: Jogo. Como funciona "O Meu Orçamento 2027"

observador.title: Jogo. O que mudava no Orçamento de 2027 de Luís Montenegro?
observador.description: É o terceiro Orçamento apresentado por Luís Montenegro. Já aprovado na generalidade passa agora para a desafiante fase da especialidade. O jogo permite-lhe mudar algumas medidas e ver o resultado.

observador.title: Estrela x Benfica. Vitória das águias foi “uma bênção”

observador.description: O FC Porto foi superior na primeira parte e chegou à vantagem aos 38 minutos, com um golo de Borja Sainz. Ainda, Acampada do Porto diz que não tem "intenção de mudar de sítio."

observador.title: Ventura exclui PSD da vitória nas próximas legislativas
observador.description: André Ventura disse que a luta pela vitória nas próximas eleições legislativas será entre o Chega e o PS e que estarão em confronto dois projetos diferentes de civilização.

observador.title: Lando vence GP do Brasil. Mercedes campeã dos construtores

observador.description: Intercalares permitiram testar mensagens e tirar o pulso ao eleitorado antes de 2028. Democratas vitoriosos arrancam na frente e favoritos republicanos tentam distanciar-se de Trump impopular.

observador.title: A escola morreu. Viva a escola!
observador.description: Aos quatro anos as crianças fazem até quatrocentas perguntas por dia. Mas será que quem gere a escola pública coloca perguntas quando avalia os seus desempenhos?

spiegel.description: Der niedersächsische CDU-Chef Lechner hat in einer Rede mehr Härte gegen kriminelle Clans gefordert – und martialische Worte gewählt. Ministerin Hamburg von den Grünen sieht darin eine verbale Entgleisung.

spiegel.title: Kim Kardashian: Kunden schimpfen über 148-Dollar-Adventskalender
spiegel.description: Kim Kardashians Modemarke »Skims« hat einen Adventskalender voller billigem Kleinkram verkauft – zu einem stattlichen Preis. In den sozialen Medien hagelt es Häme und Spott. Jetzt reagiert das Unternehmen.

spiegel.title: Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang entschuldigt sich für Affäre mit mutmaßlicher Spionin
spiegel.description: »Ich war meiner Frau untreu«: Nvidia-Chef Huang hat einen Seitensprung zugegeben, der Konzern leitet eine Untersuchung ein. Seine Geliebte arbeitete offenbar für Chinas Geheimdienst. US-Außenminister Rubio soll vor ihr gewarnt haben.

spiegel.title: Österreich: 61-jähriger Deutscher stirbt bei Wingsuit-Unfall
spiegel.description: Er galt als erfahren, doch nach dem Absprung brach der Kontakt ab: Ein deutscher Wingsuit-Flieger ist in Österreich tödlich verunglückt. Er wurde leblos auf einer Wiese aufgefunden.

spiegel.title: Formel 1: Lando Norris siegt in São Paulo, Mercedes jubelt über Team-WM
spiegel.description: Eine durcheinandergewirbelte Startaufstellung und Regenchaos versprachen Spannung. Immer wieder verloren die Fahrer auf der nassen Fahrbahn die Kontrolle. Doch einholen konnte Lando Norris am Ende niemand.

spiegel.title: Gazastreifen: Zelte versinken im Wasser – Vertriebene ohne Schutz

phys-org.title: Why the tropics lose the most birds when cities expand

phys-org.title: Personalized savings reminders can help boost retirement savings

phys-org.title: Student finds proof of rare wild cat in northern New Mexico

phys-org.title: The hidden ways insects support animal life—from habitat to health—go way beyond being food

proj-syn.title: The Economic Toll of Israel’s Wars
proj-syn.description: Israel’s economy may look strong, but three years of war have inflicted far greater damage than its robust stock market and appreciating currency suggest. Defense spending and government borrowing have risen sharply, while falling output and investment point to a prolonged recession.

proj-syn.title: Rebalancing Nature’s Books
proj-syn.description: The first report card on the implementation of the Kunming-Montreal framework was issued at this year’s UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan, and the marks were dismal. The problem is not a lack of targets, but a global financial system that pays to destroy nature and penalizes those who protect it.

proj-syn.title: Only Israel’s Arab Parties Can Restore Its Democracy
proj-syn.description: While Israel’s recent election did not deliver the transformation for which many might have hoped, it could open the way to restoring Israeli democracy. By building a coalition with the Arab-led parties, the opposition bloc could defeat not only Benjamin Netanyahu but also the violent, racist ideology he embodies.

proj-syn.title: Making the Most of America’s Midterm Tsunami
proj-syn.description: American voters’ demand for the rule of law and democracy has helped destroy Trump’s MAGA movement. Affordability may have ranked first among their concerns, but addressing it will depend on repairing and improving democratic institutions.

proj-syn.title: AI Can Help Governments Help Citizens
proj-syn.description: In developing economies, the AI debate has focused less on frontier risk and more on how to ensure that the technology actually serves people. That will require not only designing AI tools to work within government, but also investing in the state capacity required to put the technology to use.

proj-syn.title: MAGA’s Midterm Defeat Won’t Change the Course of History
proj-syn.description: The world must not succumb to euphoria following Donald Trump’s latest defeat. If anything, his lame-duck status deprives Americans and everyone else of an excuse for avoiding hard conversations about the truly radical changes that will be needed to avert future catastrophes.

proj-syn.title: Can AI Colonialism Be Prevented?
proj-syn.description: As the United States and China cement their technological dominance, the AI revolution threatens to reproduce the colonial dynamics of the first Industrial Revolution. To avoid digital colonization, middle powers must work together to build an open AI stack and establish common standards to govern it.

proj-syn.title: Turning Sub-Saharan Africa’s Cities Into Job Engines
proj-syn.description: Cities and towns will be central to creating more and better jobs for Sub-Saharan Africa’s fast-growing population, simply because the region’s people and economic activity are increasingly concentrated there. But unlocking urbanization’s potential requires policy guidance and well-planned investment.

proj-syn.title: Why Are Indian Protesters Targeting the Electoral Commission?
proj-syn.description: Following a “special intensive revision” that struck 130 million voters from the electoral rolls, India’s youth have mounted large-scale protests against the Election Commission. Given the convergence of protests with the formal political opposition, the Commission is unlikely to avoid accountability for mass disenfranchisement.

proj-syn.title: Why Aren’t We Investing More in Climate Adaptation?
proj-syn.description: There are many proven ways to protect people and assets from extreme weather, and such measures often prevent economic losses worth many times their cost. But ensuring their implementation requires making them more affordable and creating innovative revenue mechanisms and financing structures.

proj-syn.title: Put the Ocean at the Center of COP31
proj-syn.description: Last year’s UN Climate Change Conference in Belém, Brazil, put forests high on the climate agenda. This month’s UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkey, can do the same for the ocean, whose warming threatens not just food and energy security but global survival.

proj-syn.title: Who's Winning (and Who's Losing) The Ocean?
proj-syn.description: Ahead of COP31, PS sat down with Peter Thomson, the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy for the Ocean, to discuss the logic of “blue” economic development. Watch as he warns of a “world on fire,” takes governments to task for kowtowing to the oil and gas industry, and explains how we can do better for future generations.

proj-syn.title: The Democrats’ Historic Duty
proj-syn.description: While Democrats have good reason to celebrate their historic midterm victory, their current elation must quickly harden into determination. Fortunately, the field for new ideas, systemic and economic, in the US will be the most open it is likely to be for decades.

proj-syn.title: Dot-Com Lessons for the AI Bubble
proj-syn.description: Anyone who lived through the internet boom and bust of the late 1990s and early 2000s should find the current AI investment cycle worryingly familiar. Heavy reliance on debt means that if investors decide to stop lending into the boom, a financial crisis will be inevitable—and far worse than the subprime-mortgage crisis in 2008.

proj-syn.title: China Is Defanging the Dollar, Not Dethroning It
proj-syn.description: China offers Iran and Russia a way to circumvent US sanctions and continue doing business. But this comes at an elevated cost, because these countries are paid in onshore, non-convertible renminbi, which they must then convert into dollars using underground financial networks—tacitly reinforcing the greenback’s dominance.

proj-syn.title: A Fatal Challenge to Mainstream Economics
proj-syn.description: The intellectual project on which mainstream economists were raised, and which still forms the backbone of textbook education, has disappeared. What remains is a pastiche of attempted patches, apologies, and corruptions of “heterodox” ideas, all peddled by exponents of an “orthodoxy” that lacks a theoretical core.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Must Bail Out France
proj-syn.description: If France is to avoid default, the European Central Bank will need to buy large amounts of its government’s bonds through the Transmission Protection Instrument. But meeting this need—and preventing a potentially disastrous eurozone sovereign-debt-crisis—will require the ECB to waive its own rules.

proj-syn.title: The Rise and Fall of Privacy
proj-syn.description: Privacy is not a natural phenomenon, but rather a historical achievement. It emerged after the Reformation and the wars of religion that followed, reached a high point during the Victorian era, and has now been eroding for decades, long before the advent of the digital economy, social media, and AI.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI, Defense And Space Tech Lead For Large Rounds
crunchbase.description: This week brought another plethora of large funding rounds for startups and growth-stage companies. Shield AI, a defense tech player focused on autonomy and virtual simulations, secured the largest financing, bringing in $2 billion. Next on the list was drone delivery provider Zipline International, which pulled in a fresh $1.5 billion.

crunchbase.title: How To Challenge A Monopoly In The AI Age
crunchbase.description: AI chip startups can challenge the sector's Goliath's by building substantially better hardware for emerging inference demands, much as Juniper challenged Cisco with a new architecture suited to the internet’s rapid growth. To win customers, writes guest author R K Anand, co-founder and chief product officer of Tensordyne, challengers must prove their advantages, make switching easy and use small, agile teams to anticipate needs that incumbents have yet to address.

crunchbase.title: General Catalyst Tops Lead Investors For October In Busy Month For US Startup Dealmaking
crunchbase.description: October was a busy month for U.S. startup funding, led by well-known venture investors with a healthy appetite for big deals. We take a look at active investor rankings across three categories: lead deal count, largest lead investments and total venture rounds.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: Nurx And Journey Clinical Co-Founders Raise $6M For Mental Health Startup Siggy
crunchbase.description: Siggy has raised $6 million in pre-seed funding to build a mental health service that uses AI to collect patients’ histories and track progress between appointments with licensed clinicians, the startup told Crunchbase News exclusively.

crunchbase.title: Dropbox Plans $350M AI Infrastructure Deal With Tigris Buy, Its Biggest Acquisition Yet
crunchbase.description: Dropbox has announced plans to acquire Tigris Data for $350 million in a transaction the company told Crunchbase News would mark its largest acquisition since its founding in 2007.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Construction Robotics Funding Soars To $1.6B, Tripling Previous Peak
crunchbase.description: Companies spanning construction and robotics have raised about $1.6 billion so far this year  — more than 4x the $389 million recorded in all of 2025 — according to Crunchbase data. The surge was driven by three companies that raised the majority of the funding.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data: Less Than 2% Of 2026 Venture Funding Went To Post-Election Red States
crunchbase.description: So far this year, less than 2% of all startup investment has gone to companies in post-election red states, a share that is much smaller than in years past due to five states shifting to purple in the most recent election.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker
crunchbase.description: Over 127,000 workers at U.S.-based tech companies were laid off in mass job cuts in 2025, per a Crunchbase News tally, and the layoffs have continued into 2026. See the latest companies to cut roles.

crunchbase.title: Most Venture Capital Is Going To Companies That Are Founded Or Led By Billionaires
crunchbase.description: More than half of all seed- through growth-stage venture capital raised in the U.S. so far in 2026 went to seven companies founded or led by men who are already billionaires. Together, these companies raised more than $260 billion in equity funding in the first 10 months of the year.

crunchbase.title: China’s Largest Startup Deal Ever Lifts Global Venture Funding To $59B In October
crunchbase.description: Global venture funding in October totaled $59 billion, a 45% jump from a year earlier, per Crunchbase data, in large part due to a record-setting $15.9 billion funding round for China’s DeepSeek.
